name: Expiration-Week Strike Pin and Monday Release
note: The attractor is the listed option strike ladder reconstructed from price alone - $1 below $25, $2.50 to $200, $5 above - and it does not move when the price does. On the Wednesday and Thursday of an expiration week, at 15:45, a name sitting in the outer part of its strike interval is faded toward the nearest strike, provided the strike is reachable (within 1.5 daily ATR); the position is closed market-on-close on expiration day and abandoned early if price runs 2 ATR further from the strike. On the session after expiration, a name that closed within 0.25% of a strike is entered in the direction of its 5-session drift measured to the Wednesday BEFORE expiration, and closed that same session - the hedging constraint released, the pre-expiration drift resumes. Two deliberate changes: the pin band is a fraction of the half-strike-interval rather than of ATR, because on a $700 index with $5 strikes the maximum possible distance to a strike is smaller than 0.4 ATR and the ATR form of the gate can never be satisfied at all; and expiration defaults to WEEKLY Fridays rather than monthly, with monthly_only in the grid, because a two-month test window contains one monthly cycle. The cross-sectional cap of ten names per side cannot be expressed by a single-symbol family and is not implemented.
source: Sophie Xiaoyan Ni, Neil D. Pearson, Allen M. Poteshman, 'Stock Price Clustering on Option Expiration Dates', University of Illinois working paper 27 Aug 2004, published Journal of Financial Economics 78 (2005) 49-87 - the 16.5bp / $9bn figures, the $5.00 and $2.50 strike grid, the third-Friday convention, the delta-hedging and manipulation mechanisms, and the citation to Klemkosky's -1% before / +0.4% after result are taken from its text. Pinning model: Marco Avellaneda and Michael Lipkin, 'A market-induced mechanism for stock pinning', Quantitative Finance 3 (2003) 417-425.
